title.en: Ebola in DR Congo hits record number of 1,000 cases
title.zh: 刚果民主共和国埃博拉病例数创纪录，达到1000例

summary.en: The Democratic Republic of Congo has reported a record 1,000 confirmed Ebola cases in the first month of an outbreak, the highest for any Ebola outbreak in Africa. Meanwhile, Kenya's health minister has announced the halt of a US-backed Ebola quarantine center.
summary.zh: 刚果民主共和国报告称，在非洲任何一次埃博拉疫情暴发的首月，确诊病例数已达到创纪录的1000例。与此同时，肯尼亚卫生部长表示，他将暂停一个由美国支持的埃博拉隔离中心。

body.zh: 刚果民主共和国是非洲埃博拉疫情爆发第一个月确诊病例数最高的国家。与此同时，肯尼亚卫生部长表示，他正在叫停美国支持的埃博拉检疫中心。 世界卫生组织 (WHO) 一名高级官员周二在日内瓦举行的新闻发布会上表示，刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 爆发的埃博拉疫情是非洲埃博拉疫情爆发第一个月以来确诊病例数最多的国家。 截至周一，官方已确认当前爆发的相对罕见的本迪布焦埃博拉病毒导致 1,000 多例病例和 267 人死亡。 世界卫生组织于 5 月 15 日正式确认疫情爆发，但专家认为疫情可能在此之前已经传播了数周或数月。 世界卫生组织的阿卜迪拉赫曼·马哈茂德上周访问了疫情中心的布尼亚治疗中心后表示：“应对措施需要扩大，以跟上疫情不断扩大的步伐——这种情况已经开始发生。” 目前，刚果东部至少三个饱受战争蹂躏的拥挤流离失所者营地也已确诊病例。 国际移民组织的阿卜杜拉耶·沃恩 (Abdoulaye Wone) 周二在日内瓦同一场新闻发布会上表示，难民营已确诊 25 例病例，其中 14 人死亡。 据美国疾病控制与预防中心称，自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，非洲各地已爆发 20 多起埃博拉疫情。 最致命的两起事件发生在西非的几内亚、塞拉利昂和利比里亚，2014 年至 2016 年间造成 11,000 人死亡，另一起事件发生在刚果，从 2018 年开始，有 2,229 人死亡。 与此同时，肯尼亚卫生部长亚丁·杜阿勒周二向肯尼亚法院保证，他已下令立即停止在空军基地建造美国支持的埃博拉检疫设施。 周一，杜阿勒因未能遵守先前暂停施工的命令，等待司法部门评估而被判藐视法庭。 位于纳纽基市中心的帐篷设施原本应该作为美国国民在刚果民主共和国疫情期间感染埃博拉病毒的治疗中心。 该项目于五月首次宣布，有时会引发暴力抗议，附近共有三人被杀。 在收到部长的保证后，法官帕特里夏·尼亚温迪·曼德（Patricia Nyaundi Mande）释放了杜阿莱，没有进一步的处罚，但警告他不要进一步不服从。 “我已指示立即完全停止任何有关莱基皮亚空军基地设施的预期建设、场地准备或相关活动，等待实质性请愿书的听证会和裁决，或直至本...

reflection.en: The news of a record Ebola outbreak in DR Congo reminds us of the profound suffering caused by disease. In such times of widespread illness and fear, we remember Yahweh, who is near to the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds. This verse offers a hopeful perspective that even amidst great pain, divine compassion is present.
reflection.zh: 刚果民主共和国埃博拉疫情病例数创纪录的消息，提醒我们疾病所带来的深重苦难。在这样广泛的疾病和恐惧时期，我们记念雅伟，他医治伤心的人，包扎他们的伤处。这节经文提供了一个充满希望的视角，即即使在巨大的痛苦中，神圣的怜悯也同在。

verse.textEn: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
verse.textZh: 他医好伤心的人，裹好他们的伤处。

title.en: Hard-right figures take aim at Ed Miliband and UK net zero policies at ‘anti-woke Davos’
title.zh: 强硬右翼人士在“反觉醒达沃斯”会议上抨击埃德·米利班德和英国净零政策

summary.en: At a conference dubbed 'anti-woke Davos,' hard-right figures, including Kemi Badenoch, joined US anti-abortion activists and European far-right parties to criticize Britain's net zero policies. The energy secretary, Ed Miliband, was specifically targeted and described as a 'villain.'
summary.zh: 在一场被称为“反觉醒达沃斯”的会议上，包括凯米·巴德诺赫在内的强硬右翼人士与美国反堕胎活动家及欧洲极右翼政党一道，批评了英国的净零政策。能源大臣埃德·米利班德成为具体攻击目标，并被描述为“恶棍”。

body.en: Kemi Badenoch, who joined US anti-abortion activists and European far-right parties at ARC, described energy secretary as a ‘villain’ Britain’s net zero policies and the energy secretary, Ed Miliband, have come under fire at a conference of conservatives, rightwing populists and wealthy US backers linked to Donald Trump . The energy policies pursued by the British government were described as a “tragic mistake” by Trump’s energy secretary, one of a number of officials from the US administration attending the event. reflection.en: In the heat of political debate, it's easy to see opponents as personal adversaries or 'villains.' This verse reminds us that our deepest struggles are often not against individuals, but against underlying ideologies or systemic forces. Cultivating this perspective can help us engage with disagreements more thoughtfully and with less personal animosity.
reflection.zh: 在激烈的政治辩论中，我们很容易将对手视为个人敌人或“恶棍”。这节经文提醒我们，我们最深层的挣扎往往不是针对个人，而是针对潜在的意识形态或系统性力量。培养这种视角可以帮助我们更深思熟虑地处理分歧，减少个人敌意。

verse.textEn: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.
verse.textZh: 因我们并不是与属血气的争战，乃是与那些执政的、掌权的、管辖这幽暗世界的，以及天空属灵气的恶魔争战。

title.en: Europe’s heatwave drives electricity prices to new highs as demand soars

summary.en: Europe is experiencing a heatwave that has significantly increased electricity demand, particularly for air conditioning and fans. This surge in demand, coupled with reduced windfarm output, has driven electricity prices to unprecedented levels across European markets, with Great Britain paying up to six times the...
summary.zh: 欧洲正经历一场热浪，导致电力需求大幅增加，尤其是空调和电扇的使用。这种需求的激增，加上风力发电量下降，使得欧洲市场的电价飙升至新高，英国为进口电力支付的价格甚至达到平时的六倍。

body.en: Great Britain has paid at least six times the normal price for imported power as millions turn on air conditioning and windfarm output sags The heatwave has prompted a sharp rise in electricity prices across European markets as millions turn to air conditioners and electric fans to battle record high temperatures, which have also caused a string of power plant outages across the continent. Great Britain imported electricity from Europe at more than six times the normal price on Tuesday as the high pressure heat dome has slowed wind speeds, hitting renewable energy generation, and caused outages at multiple gas plants across the country. reflection.en: As heatwaves strain energy grids and drive up prices, many face the challenge of increased costs for essential cooling. Habakkuk 3:17-18 reminds us that even when resources are scarce and circumstances are difficult, we can find joy and strength in Yahweh. This perspective encourages us to seek resilience and hope beyond immediate material comforts.
reflection.zh: 当热浪给电网带来压力并推高电价时，许多人面临着为基本降温支付更高费用的挑战。哈巴谷书3:17-18提醒我们，即使资源匮乏、环境艰难，我们仍能在雅伟里面找到喜乐和力量。这种视角鼓励我们在眼前的物质舒适之外寻求韧性和盼望。

verse.textEn: Though the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines... yet I will rejoice in Yahweh.
verse.textZh: 虽然无花果树不发旺，葡萄树不结果……然而，我要因雅伟欢欣。

Rubio is to meet Gulf allies on Tuesday and Wednesday in an attempt to reassure them that the US remains committed to their security and the 60-day ceasefire deal struck with Iran last week will not embolden Tehran. reflection.en: In a world often marked by tension and competing interests, diplomatic efforts to maintain open waterways and regional stability reflect a commitment to peace. Yahweh calls us to live at peace with everyone, as far as it depends on us, actively seeking understanding and de-escalation in complex situations.
reflection.zh: 在一个常被紧张和利益冲突所困扰的世界里，旨在维护开放航道和地区稳定的外交努力，体现了对和平的承诺。雅伟呼召我们，只要力所能及，就要与所有人和平相处，在复杂的局势中积极寻求理解和缓和。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Lebanon's lose-lose: Is there another way out of conflict?
title.zh: 黎巴嫩的双输：还有其他摆脱冲突的出路吗？

summary.en: The new US-Iran peace deal seems to be forcing Lebanon to choose between Israel's sphere of influence or Iran's. It wants neither. But could there be a better alternative, achieved with the help of regional diplomacy?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The new US-Iran peace deal seems to be forcing Lebanon to choose between Israel's sphere of influence or Iran's. It wants neither. But could there be a better alternative, achieved with the help of regional diplomacy?

As representatives of the Lebanese government begin another round of talks with their Israeli counterparts in Washington this week, their country finds itself in an increasingly impossible situation.

In Lebanon , fighting between local militant group Hezbollah and neighboring Israel has displaced over a million people, killed thousands and caused around $1.4 billion (€1.2 billion) worth of damage. 

Israel says it plans to stay in what it is calling a "security buffer zone" there so its own citizens in northern Israel are safe from Hezbollah attacks.

Iran, which supports Hezbollah in Lebanon, wants fighting there to stop and has made respect for Lebanese sovereignty a condition of the memorandum of understanding it signed last week with the US. The memorandum halted the Iran-US-Israel war that started in late February.

This is why the Lebanese government sees Iran's tactic, of bringing it into the peace deal, as an infringement on its own sovereignty. Lebanon has been trying to negotiate an end to the conflict with Israel directly. The two have been discussing how to neutralize Hezbollah . Critics of the talks, another round of which is taking place in Washington between June 23 and 25, say that what Israel wants would leave Lebanon beholden to its neighbor and that if the Lebanese army were forced to confront Hezbollah directly, that could spark a new civil war in Lebanon.

All of which has left Lebanon with a difficult choice: Iran or Israel? Neither option offers much chance of lasting peace or economic recovery for the small Mediterranean nation.

Michael Young, a senior editor at the Carnegie Middle East Center in Beirut, believes there might be an alternative. In a June 18 commentary, he wrote about the potential of a solution first presented by Egyptian diplomats late last year. The Egyptian proposal, or framework, has been getting increasing support from other countries in the region, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Turkey as well as Pakistan, in a mediator role.

The countries involved, Young writes, want neither Iran nor Israel to dominate the region.

The Egyptian-backed framework "outlines a three-phase process of 'organized, gradual transition'," for Hezbollah, Young explains.

This includes ending the group's cross-border activities, integrating Hezbollah fighters into Lebanon's army and Hezbollah social services into the Lebanese state. The end result would be the "transformation of Hezbollah into an exclusively political and civilian entity."

body.zh: 新的美伊和平协议似乎迫使黎巴嫩在以色列的势力范围和伊朗的势力范围之间做出选择。它两者都不想要。但是否有更好的选择，通过区域外交来实现？ 随着黎巴嫩政府代表本周在华盛顿与以色列同行开始新一轮会谈，黎巴嫩发现自己陷入了越来越不可能的境地。 在黎巴嫩，当地激进组织真主党与邻国以色列之间的战斗已导致超过一百万人流离失所，数千人死亡，并造成价值约 14 亿美元（12 亿欧元）的损失。 以色列表示，计划留在所谓的“安全缓冲区”，以便以色列北部的本国公民免受真主党的袭击。 支持黎巴嫩真主党的伊朗希望停止那里的战斗，并将尊重黎巴嫩主权作为其上周与美国签署的谅解备忘录的条件。该备忘录终止了二月底开始的伊朗、美国和以色列战争。 这就是为什么黎巴嫩政府认为伊朗将其纳入和平协议的策略是对其主权的侵犯。黎巴嫩一直试图通过直接谈判结束与以色列的冲突。两人一直在讨论如何压制真主党。 新一轮会谈将于 6 月 23 日至 25 日在华盛顿举行，批评人士表示，以色列希望让黎巴嫩对其邻国负有责任，如果黎巴嫩军队被迫直接对抗真主党，可能会在黎巴嫩引发新的内战。 所有这些都让黎巴嫩面临着艰难的选择：伊朗还是以色列？对于这个地中海小国来说，这两种选择都没有多大机会实现持久和平或经济复苏。 贝鲁特卡内基中东中心的高级编辑迈克尔·杨认为可能还有其他选择。在 6 月 18 日的评论中，他谈到了埃及外交官去年年底首次提出的解决方案的潜力。埃及的提议或框架得到了该地区其他国家越来越多的支持，包括沙特阿拉伯、卡塔尔和土耳其以及发挥调解作用的巴基斯坦。 杨写道，相关国家都不希望伊朗和以色列主宰该地区。 杨解释说，埃及支持的框架“概述了真主党‘有组织、逐步过渡’的三个阶段过程”。 这包括结束该组织的跨境活动，将真主党战士纳入黎巴嫩军队，并将真主党社会服务纳入黎巴嫩国家。最终结果将是“真主党转变为纯粹的政治和民事实体”。 同时，该框架还需要...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Ransom note claims Nancy Guthrie died after abduction
title.zh: 勒索信声称南希·格思里在绑架后死亡

summary.en: On Tuesday, Today show presenter Savannah Guthrie begged anyone with information to come forward, saying, "We are in agony."
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A ransom note sent days after the 84-year-old mother of US presenter Savannah Guthrie was abducted from her home claimed she had died, according to investigators.

The note was one of two addressed to Nancy Guthrie's family and sent to news media in the days after her January kidnapping.

The first demanded millions in bitcoin for her release, but the second stated that she had died, according to sources cited by US media.

The note from the possible kidnappers reportedly stated they did not mean for her to die and included an apology to the family. The Pima County Sheriff's Department declined to comment on the contents of the notes, but said the investigation "remains active and ongoing".

On Tuesday morning, during her first appearance on NBC's Today show since news of the second ransom note dropped, Savannah Guthrie addressed the news as tears fell from her face.

The longtime television presenter again begged people with information to come forward: "Somebody knows something," she said. "We are in agony."

"This is a new story today that is on your radar, but this is the life we live every day," Guthrie added.

When asked about the case by reporters on Tuesday, US President Donald Trump said that he hopes they find her and that the Guthrie family "has gone through hell".

The FBI and Pima County have spent months investigating the elder Guthrie's mysterious abduction from her home near Tucson, Arizona.

"The Pima County Sheriff's Department continues to work closely with the FBI as investigators follow up on leads, review information, and pursue the facts surrounding this case," a spokesperson for the sheriff's department said.

The FBI declined to comment on the contents of the ransom notes or whether investigators had found any evidence that Guthrie had died.

The BBC's US partner CBS and other outlets reported on Monday that law enforcement had requested that media hold off publishing details of the notes while they investigated Guthrie's disappearance.

"CBS News was aware of that second note, and was aware of the contents of the second note, but there was a real concern about messing up an investigation that was at a very sensitive time," journalist Anna Schecter said on CBS's streaming platform on Tuesday.

Schecter noted concerns that putting out the information could slow the momentum of the public's help - searching through their security videos or looking for anything suspicious in their neighbourhoods.

"That was really the reason why those of us journalists who were following this very closely did not report this at the time," she said.

body.zh: 据调查人员称，美国主持人萨凡纳·格思里 (Savannah Guthrie) 84 岁的母亲在家中被绑架，几天后，一封勒索信发出，并声称她已经死亡。 这张纸条是写给南希·格思里家人的两封信之一，并在她一月份被绑架后几天发送给新闻媒体。 据美国媒体援引消息人士称，第一人要求支付数百万比特币才能释放她，但第二人声称她已经死亡。 据报道，可能的绑架者在纸条上表示，他们并不是故意要她死，并向家人道歉。皮马县治安部门拒绝对笔记的内容发表评论，但表示调查“仍在积极进行中”。 周二早上，自第二张勒索信的消息传出以来，萨凡娜·格思里 (Savannah Guthrie) 首次出现在 NBC 的《今日》节目中，她在谈到这一消息时泪流满面。 这位长期担任电视主持人的人再次恳求知情者提供信息：“有人知道一些事情，”她说。 “我们正处于痛苦之中。” “这是今天你们关注的一个新故事，但这就是我们每天的生活，”格思里补充道。 周二，当记者问及此案时，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，他希望他们能找到她，并表示格思里一家“已经经历了地狱”。 联邦调查局和皮马县花了几个月的时间调查老格思里在亚利桑那州图森附近的家中被神秘绑架的事件。 皮马县治安部门发言人表示：“皮马县治安部门将继续与联邦调查局密切合作，调查人员会跟进线索、审查信息并追查与此案相关的事实。” 联邦调查局拒绝就赎金单的内容或调查人员是否发现格思里死亡的任何证据发表评论。 英国广播公司的美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司和其他媒体周一报道称，执法部门要求媒体在调查格思里失踪事件期间暂缓公布这些笔记的细节。 记者安娜·谢克特周二在哥伦比亚广播公司的流媒体平台上表示：“哥伦比亚广播公司新闻知道第二封信，也知道第二封信的内容，但确实担心在非常敏感的时刻搞砸调查。” 谢克特指出，担心公布这些信息可能会减缓公众提供帮助的势头——搜索他们的安全视频或寻找社区中任何可疑的东西。 “这确实是我们这些密切关注此事的记者当时没有报道此事的原因，”她说。 1 月 31 日，南希·格思里 (Nancy Guthrie) 被亲戚送回家后失踪。当她接下来没有去朋友家观看虚拟周日教堂礼拜时，人们越来越担心……

body.en:
Polish President Karol Nawrocki last week stripped Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Poland's highest state honor. How did it come to this? And what has it got to do with next year's election in Poland?

The political and military support Ukraine received from Poland made a major contribution to Ukraine's ability to successfully defend itself in the early days of Russia's full-scale invasion, which began in February 2022.

Now, however, a dispute about the past, which has been rumbling on for weeks, is plunging the two neighbors into an ever-deepening crisis.

On Friday evening, Polish President Karol Nawrocki announced on X that he was revoking the Order of the White Eagle, Poland's highest state honor, from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy .

In doing so, Nawrocki made good on a threat he made several weeks previously during the dispute about the name given to a Ukrainian special forces unit, "Heroes of the UPA."

"We believed that the Order of the White Eagle, awarded in 2023, was meant for the Ukrainian People and our army. That is what was said at the time. Today, I sent the Order back to the President of Poland," Zelenskyy wrote on his social media accounts on Saturday.

He thanked Poland for its support and solidarity thus far and said that since the honor had also been bestowed on Russian Empress Catherine II, Italian dictator Benito Mussolini and former German chancellor Gerhard Schröder, "we in Ukraine will not argue with this."

He also posted photos without comments showing him sending the order back to Nawrocki via the private Ukrainian postal and courier service Nova Post.

Speaking in an interview with the Ukrainian television channel 1+1, Zelenskyy later accused his Polish counterpart of having taken the step because of next year's parliamentary election in Poland.

"President Karol Nawrocki is fighting for the position of his party against the prime minister [Donald Tusk]. It is the same thing that [former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor] Orban did. It is the wrong way. I think it will end badly," said Zelenskyy.

Over the weekend, there was an almost united response from politicians in Ukraine.

Three of the country's four living former presidents — Leonid Kuchma, Viktor Yushchenko and Petro Poroshenko — returned their Polish orders. The fourth, the pro-Russian Viktor Yanukovych , fled to Russia in 2014.

Presidential Chief of Staff Kyrylo Budanov and Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha also returned their honors.

"Nawrocki has become the destroyer of the positive progress we have made in recent times. It's not for nothing that he receives applause from Moscow," said Sybiha, adding, "No president of another country will dictate our history to us."

title.en: Zambia ex-president's family wins latest legal battle over what should happen to his body
title.zh: 赞比亚前总统的家人在关于他的尸体应该如何处理的最新法律诉讼中获胜

summary.en: Edgar Lungu's family and the Zambian government remained in dispute 12 months after he died.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
More than a year after the death of Zambia's former President Edgar Lungu, his family have won their appeal to have his body buried in South Africa where he died - overturning a high court ruling that allowed the Zambian government to repatriate the corpse.

Tuesday's Supreme Court of Appeal judgement finally puts to rest the legal battle over what should happen to his remains following a long-standing feud between Lungu and his successor, President Hakainde Hichilema.

The Zambian government has said while it disagrees with the ruling it will "not be taking the matter any further".

It had long argued that, as a former head of state, Lungu should be honoured in the country.

The Zambian government wished to see him laid to rest alongside his predecessors in the special presidential burial ground in the capital, Lusaka.

But Lungu's family wanted a private burial after negotiations with the government over the funeral arrangements broke down.

"The very ritual intended to bring closure has, instead, pitted family against the state in a hard-fought legal dispute far from the protagonists' home," said Justice Raylene May Keightley in Tuesday's judgement.

Last August, the South African high court in Pretoria ruled that Zambia's government could repatriate the body and give him a state funeral - an outcome that left Lungu's relatives visibly distraught in the courtroom.

The family appealed against the decision but, in a surprise announcement in April Zambia's government said Lungu's remains had been "formally transferred" to the state by the South African court.

But just a few hours later, the same South African court ordered the Zambian government to return the body until the matter went to court again.

The former president died of an undisclosed illness aged 68 at a clinic in Pretoria. Chaos ensued following his death, with mourners receiving conflicting information from the government and Lungu's political party , the Patriotic Front (PF).

Two separate mourning periods were announced and at one point there were competing condolence books.

Lungu, who led Zambia from 2015 until 2021, had numerous rows with Hichilema, who was the opposition leader for many years before finally unseating his bitter rival.

After Lungu's death, his family said the ex-president did not want Hichilema to be at his funeral or "anywhere near" his body.

In this latest ruling at the Supreme Court of Appeal, the judges said it was clear that the former president "viewed himself to be persona non grata in his own country" of Zambia and "felt that he would not be afforded a dignified send-off" if his successor was present.
body.zh: 赞比亚前总统埃德加·伦古去世一年多后，他的家人赢得了上诉，将他的尸体埋在南非，推翻了高等法院允许赞比亚政府遣返尸体的裁决。 在伦古与其继任者哈坎德·希奇莱马总统之间长期不和之后，周二最高法院的判决最终平息了关于他的遗体如何处理的法律斗争。 赞比亚政府表示，虽然不同意这一裁决，但“不会再进一步​​处理此事”。 长期以来，人们一直认为，作为前国家元首，伦古应该在该国受到尊重。 赞比亚政府希望看到他与前任总统一起安葬在首都卢萨卡的特别总统墓地。 但在与政府就葬礼安排的谈判破裂后，伦古的家人希望举行私人葬礼。 法官雷琳·梅·凯特利在周二的判决中表示：“这个原本旨在结束的仪式，却让家人与国家在远离主角家的地方展开了一场激烈的法律纠纷。” 去年八月，南非比勒陀利亚高等法院裁定赞比亚政府可以遣返尸体并为他举行国葬——这一结果让伦古的亲属在法庭上明显心烦意乱。 伦古的家人对这一决定提出上诉，但赞比亚政府在四月出人意料地宣布，伦古的遗体已被南非法院“正式转移”到该州。 但仅仅几个小时后，同一家南非法院命令赞比亚政府归还尸体，直到此事再次上法庭。 这位前总统因未公开的疾病在比勒陀利亚的一家诊所去世，享年 68 岁。他去世后，混乱随之而来，哀悼者从政府和伦古的政党爱国阵线（PF）收到相互矛盾的信息。 宣布了两个不同的哀悼期，并且一度出现了相互竞争的吊唁簿。 伦古从 2015 年到 2021 年领导赞比亚，他与多年担任反对党领袖的希奇莱马发生了多次争执，最后最终推翻了他的死对头。 伦古去世后，他的家人表示，前总统不希望希奇莱马参加他的葬礼或“靠近”他的尸体。 在最高法院上诉法院的最新裁决中，法官们表示，很明显，这位前总统“认为自己在赞比亚自己的国家是不受欢迎的人”，并且“认为如果他的继任者在场，他将不会得到有尊严的送行”。

body.zh: 彼得·穆雷尔承认在担任苏格兰民族党首席执行官期间挪用资金。他掌握着苏格兰民族党的财政权，而他当时的妻子尼古拉·斯特金 (Nicola Sturgeon) 则担任苏格兰首席部长。 苏格兰民族党 (SNP) 前首席执行官彼得·穆雷尔 (Peter Murrell) 周二被判入狱五年多，他承认挪用了超过 40 万英镑（按当前汇率计算，约合 465,000 欧元或 530,000 美元）的党资金，用于购买房车、汽车和豪华家居用品等物品。 61 岁的默雷尔是前苏格兰民族党党魁尼古拉·斯特金 (Nicola Sturgeon) 现已分居的丈夫，斯特金于 2023 年突然辞去苏格兰首席部长职务，几个月后她因苏格兰民族党财务调查而被捕。 去年三月，她被洗清了无不当行为的罪名。 这对夫妇在苏格兰民族党中担任双重角色，斯特金是近十年来苏格兰民族党最资深的政治家，而穆雷尔则负责党的管理，甚至在这些罪行为公众所知之前就引发了适当性的问题。 穆雷尔上个月在爱丁堡高等法院承认在 2010 年至 2023 年间挪用苏格兰民族党资金，用这笔钱购买了一辆大众汽车，后来又购买了一辆捷豹汽车，以及雅诗兰黛、Harrods 和 LeCreuset 等奢侈品牌的商品。 周二，法官安德鲁·杨判处他五年零三个月监禁。 “你的行为严重违反了对你所领导的组织、个人成员和捐助者的信任，”杨在法庭上告诉穆雷尔。 “这是一起精心策划的不诚实罪。让我向你澄清，我今天判处的判决的一个因素是对其他大型组织的任何高级官员起到威慑作用，他们可能会像你一样滥用职权，”法官说。 当局现在将寻求通过犯罪所得法律诉讼追回被盗用的资金。 “事实上，很难清楚地了解是什么驱动了你的行为，”杨说。 “你得到的很多高价值物品根本就没有使用过。” 此案给支持独立的政党带来了尴尬的问题，该党主导苏格兰政坛近二十年。然而，在很大程度上要归功于英国首相凯尔·斯塔默和工党的努力，苏格兰民族党得以在上个月的苏格兰议会选举中重整旗鼓，并继续保持最强政党的地位。 尽管斯特金去年被警方和检察官洗清没有任何不当行为，但她声称“不知道也不怀疑他将苏格兰民族党的资金用于个人目的”的说法仍然存在疑问。 与箱子相连的小但价值较低的物品——比如她的吊坠……

title.en: Israeli troops kill two in south Lebanon after lull in fighting, authorities say
title.zh: 当局称，以色列军队在战斗平息后在黎巴嫩南部打死两人

summary.en: Israel's military says the two men were Hezbollah operatives, but the Iran-backed group accuses it of a ceasefire violation.

body.en:
Israeli soldiers have shot dead two people in southern Lebanon, the Lebanese health ministry says, in the first fatal incident reported since the latest ceasefire between Israel and the Iran-backed armed group Hezbollah appeared to take hold at the weekend.

Lebanon's state-run National News Agency said two men were killed while they were standing near a bulldozer that was unblocking a road in the town of Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

Israel's military said soldiers in the Ali al-Taher ridge area, just east of Nabatieh al-Fawqa, fired at "four Hezbollah terrorists riding a bulldozer and a motorcycle" who posed a threat.

It added that the group had crossed into the Israeli-declared "security zone" in southern Lebanon and ignored warning shots from the soldiers.

The Israeli military also said that, in a separate incident, soldiers struck a "cell of armed terrorists" north of the security zone. It released a photo that it said showed one of the men holding a rifle. There were no immediate reports of any casualties.

NNA identified the two men killed in Nabatieh al-Fawqa as Mohammed Amhaz and Sajed al-Hajj Ali. It said they were with a team from the Islamic Health Association, an emergency service linked to Hezbollah, and a bulldozer that was working to reopen roads and recover bodies underneath rubble in the al-Deir neighbourhood.

Hezbollah's military wing, the Islamic Resistance, said in a statement: "What the enemy has committed constitutes a blatant violation of the ceasefire, which the Resistance has adhered to up to this point". It did not say whether the group would retaliate.

Ali al-Taher ridge, which overlooks much of south-eastern Lebanon including the major town of Nabatieh, has been one of the most fiercely contested positions in the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah.

Israeli ground forces attempted to seize the ridge - where they believe there is a Hezbollah "underground military fortress" - in the days before the new ceasefire deal was announced. Four soldiers were killed in a Hezbollah attack on their tank in the nearby village of Kfar Tebnit early on Friday.

The Israeli military responded by carrying out more than 150 air strikes on what it said were Hezbollah targets. The Lebanese health ministry said 83 people were killed.

On Friday afternoon, the US said Israel and Hezbollah had agreed to a ceasefire, following concerns that the continued fighting in Lebanon would undermine the preliminary agreement ending the war between the US, Israel and Iran.

However, another 20 people were killed in fresh Israeli air strikes across Lebanon on Saturday, according to the country's civil defence agency.

title.en: Have World Cup changes made final group stage games unfair?
title.zh: 世界杯的变化是否让小组赛最后的比赛变得不公平？

summary.en: With eight teams already having nothing to play for, has the jeopardy in the group stage at the World Cup been diminished? And are concerns over the integrity of competition justified?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The group stage of the 2026 World Cup always felt as though it might lack jeopardy.

After all, with 32 of 48 teams advancing to the knockout rounds it is more difficult to be eliminated than to qualify.

But the impact of two key changes are perhaps only now being realised by fans as the second round of matches comes to an end.

They are the first ever World Cup using head-to-head records instead of goal difference as the primary tiebreaker for countries level on points.

And the second is this World Cup will feature a third-placed table for the first time since 1994 as teams vie for the eight remaining slots.

Head-to-head means teams can either win a group or be eliminated after two games.

For instance, Argentina have six points and cannot be overtaken in Group J because they have beaten the two teams on three points, Austria and Algeria.

Likewise, Jordan on zero points have been eliminated because they have lost to those two teams.

If goal difference were being used first every team would still have something on the line.

Will countries with nothing to play for field weaker teams in their final game as a result?

As for the third-placed table, because there are so many groups it takes five days to complete the final round of matches.

That means, for example, when Scotland play Brazil on Wednesday (23:00 BST) they will have no idea what the cut-off in terms of a points threshold will be to go through in third.

A team playing on Saturday or Sunday will likely know exactly what they require.

Using head to head as the first tiebreaker is nothing new. Uefa favours it in all its competitions.

The theory behind it is how it separates teams on the result of the match between them, filtering out potentially big scorelines from other matches which can skew goal difference.

Although half the size in terms of the number of teams competing, since 2016, the Euros has used the same format as the World Cup with some third-placed teams qualifying.

At Euro 2016, Italy topped the group and Ukraine were knocked out after two games.

At Euro 2020 it happened in one group, creating a dead rubber between Netherlands and North Macedonia.

Yet more teams have already been either eliminated or made it through to the round of 32 at this World Cup (eight) than in the whole of the three Euros combined (seven).

USA v Turkey and Argentina v Jordan are dead rubbers, fixtures between group winners and eliminated teams.

More could follow on Tuesday. England/Ghana and Colombia could seal top spot, while Croatia/Panama and Uzbekistan might go out.

title.en: Colombia: The 'Tiger's' victory signals a rightward shift
title.zh: 哥伦比亚：“老虎”的胜利标志着右倾

summary.en: With the election of Abelardo de la Espriella, an ultra-right-wing outsider has won the presidential runoff in Colombia for the first time. The tight victory marks a political shift and could trigger new conflicts.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
With the election of Abelardo de la Espriella, an ultra-right-wing outsider has won the presidential runoff in Colombia for the first time. The tight victory marks a political shift and could trigger new conflicts.

Colombia has elected a new president, and the result has the potential to transform the country for the long term. According to preliminary results, far-right lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella has won the presidential runoff  by a narrow margin with 49.66% of the vote, edging out the left-wing ruling party candidate Ivan Cepeda, who received 48.7%. 

The margin of about 250,000 votes is the narrowest in the history of Colombian presidential elections.

De la Espriella, a 47-year-old lawyer, entrepreneur and political newcomer, will succeed Gustavo Petro , the country's first left-wing president. For Colombia , this will likely mean a significant shift to the right and a departure from key initiatives of the previous administration, particularly in the areas of peace, security, energy and social policy. At the same time, de la Espriella is taking over a country that is politically deeply divided.

The actual takeaway from this election lies less in the result than in the narrow margin between the candidates: Nearly half of the voters supported Petro's current course , while the other half favored a fundamental change in direction.

"Colombia has voted, and it could hardly have been closer," Kristin Wesemann, head of the German Konrad Adenauer Foundation's office in Bogota, told DW.

"Politically, the country is split almost evenly," she said, "and the real challenge begins now in governing a deeply divided country and meeting the high expectations for greater security, economic stability and a government capable of taking action."

Sabine Kurtenbach, interim president of the German Institute for Global and Area Studies (GIGA), offers a similar assessment of the election results.

What the country needs now, according to Kurtenbach, is "a president who tries to build bridges and who does not further fuel this polarization."

Viviana Garcia Pinzon of the Arnold Bergstraesser Institute also told DW that the country is shaped by "two very different social models." The result shows "very clearly how divided the country is." 

De la Espriella is by no means a traditional politician. He first became known as a criminal defense attorney representing high-profile clients, including paramilitary leaders and alleged drug traffickers. Later, he made a name for himself as an entrepreneur, television personality and commentator. His public persona is provocative and media-savvy.

body.en:
United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced he will step down as leader of the Labour Party and leave office within weeks, ending a government that swept to power in a landslide election victory less than two years ago.

Starmer said he will remain in Downing Street as caretaker prime minister until Labour chooses a replacement, setting in motion another leadership transition in a country that has cycled through prime ministers at remarkable speed in the post-Brexit era.

The decision follows months of mounting political pressure , deteriorating public support and growing concern within Labour that the government had lost the confidence of voters.

Speaking outside Number 10 on Monday, an emotional Starmer said he had informed King Charles III of his intention to resign and would work to ensure an orderly transfer of power.

"Every decision I have taken has been about putting the country I love first," he said.

His departure makes him the sixth UK prime minister in a decade to announce an early exit.

Starmer entered office in July 2024 with one of Labour's strongest election victories in decades.

After 14 years of Conservative government, Labour promised political stability, economic repair and a reset of public trust.

Starmer’s leadership became increasingly defined by domestic policy reversals, public frustration over cost of living pressures and criticism that Labour had failed to deliver visible change despite its commanding parliamentary majority.

Several ministerial departures and internal dissatisfaction fuelled concerns the government lacked direction.

Labour also faced pressure from outside parliament, with the anti-immigration Reform UK party gaining support and reshaping political debate.

The pressure intensified following poor local and regional election results in May, prompting questions within Labour about whether Starmer remained the right person to lead the party into the next general election, expected in 2029.

While Starmer had publicly insisted he intended to continue, reports emerged that senior figures had privately urged him to step aside and allow Labour to reset before support eroded further.

In his resignation speech, Starmer said he accepted that colleagues believed a change in leadership was necessary.

Attention has quickly turned to who could become the UK's next prime minister, with former Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham confirming he will seek the Labour leadership.

title.en: 'Unprecedented': Is this the moment US-Israel ties stopped being 'special'?
title.zh: “前所未有”：现在是美以关系不再“特殊”的时刻吗？

summary.en: Donald Trump and his vice president's remarks about Israel have left some wondering if US-Israeli relations are irrevocably changed.

body.en:
At the White House press briefing room, the United States vice president JD Vance recently delivered a scathing rebuke to Israeli cabinet ministers critical of the United States' deal with Iran .

"Donald J Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment in time," he said late last week.

"If I was in the cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world."

It was, in some respects, extraordinary. US leaders have previously expressed frustration — even sworn — at Israeli officials in private. But the comments from Vance so publicly putting Israeli officials in their place were unexpected.

"Since really the Eisenhower administration [1953-1961], the United States has tended to criticise Israel behind closed doors, not in public, so this criticism in public is fairly unprecedented," Brendon O'Connor, a professor of US Politics and US Foreign Relations, told SBS News.

The comments, along with plummeting American public sentiment towards Israel and the war in Iran , have raised questions about the future of what has been dubbed as the "special relationship".

Trita Parsi, executive vice president at the Washington-based Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, says the Trump administration is taking the first steps toward "de-specialising" the US-Israel relationship.

"What the administration is doing now is beginning to be what I would think is the contours of a deep specialisation of the US-Israeli relationship, meaning that it is a very important relationship, but it is downgraded to being at the same level as the US has with France, for instance," he told CNN.

In June, US President Donald Trump called Netanyahu "f---ing crazy" over Israel's military escalation in Lebanon. Last week, he said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had "no f---ing judgment" after Israeli strikes targeted Beirut amid ongoing Iran war negotiations.

This may be the first time that a sitting US president has publicly attacked an Israeli prime minister, but it's not the first instance in private. Bill Clinton, for example, is said to have been incensed after a 1996 meeting with Netanyahu, reportedly telling aides: "Who the f--- does he think he is?"

More recently, then president Joe Biden is reported to have called Netanyahu a "f---ing liar" about a Gaza military decision.

title.en: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announces resignation after months of party pressure
title.zh: 英国首相基尔·斯塔默在数月党内压力后宣布辞职

summary.en: The UK prime minister announced his resignation after facing months of pressure from his party, stating his commitment to ensuring a smooth transition of power.
summary.zh: 英国首相在面临数月党内压力后宣布辞职，并表示将尽力确保权力有序过渡。

body.en:
United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer says he will resign, with a new leader to be in place by the time UK parliament returns in September, paving the way for Britain to have its seventh leader in 10 years.

In an emotional speech on Monday, Starmer said he had listened to his governing Labour Party and realised he was no longer the person to lead it into a national election in 2029.

After spending weeks saying he would fight any challenge to his position as prime minister, Starmer spent the weekend reflecting on his political future at his country residence, watching his support in the party drain away.

Outside his office and London residence on Downing Street, Starmer said he would ask the Labour Party's organising committee to set out a timeline for a leadership contest to find his replacement.

Nominations would open on 9 July, close by mid-July, and if there is a contest, a new leader will be in place by September. He did not mention his rival, Andy Burnham, who is widely expected to replace him.

"The question my party is asking now is whether I am best placed to lead us into the next general election. I have heard the answer from my parliamentary party to that question and I accept that answer with good grace," he said.

After describing the achievements his government had secured in his two years of power, a man who was often criticised for being robotic, became visibly emotional, his voice cracking when he thanked his family for their support.

"When I leave the biggest job in the country, I will spend more time on the most important job, being the best husband I can to my fantastic wife, Vic, who has been a rock by my side through good times and bad, and being the best dad I can to my beautiful children, who are my pride and my joy."

Whoever replaces Starmer will become the UK's seventh prime minister since the Brexit vote to leave the European Union, which took place 10 years ago this week.

That level of turnover — the highest in the UK in nearly two centuries — underlines the struggle of maintaining the support of voters angry at successive failures to improve living standards, public services and tackle illegal immigration.

The threat to Starmer, which had been building for months, increased sharply on Friday when Burnham, the Greater Manchester mayor , decisively won a parliamentary election to return to Westminster, beating a candidate from Nigel Farage's Reform UK party, which has led national opinion polls for more than a year.

title.en: Europe had a 'Trump whisperer'. Now it may have no one with his ear

summary.en: A key European relationship with Donald Trump is under strain as he trades blows with Italy's Giorgia Meloni.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
When Donald Trump returned to the White House last year, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni was the only European leader to attend the inauguration.

Seventeen months later, their relationship is publicly breaking down, as the two right-wing leaders trade barbs on social media.

Trump's relationships with traditional European allies have further strained in his second term, and he's become increasingly unpopular among voters in much of Western Europe.

He's clashed with leaders including Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over his decision to go to war with Iran.

And earlier this year, he shattered trust within the NATO military alliance with threats to take over Greenland.

The deterioration of the relationship with Meloni raises questions about who, if anyone, still has the US president's ear in Europe.

Meloni was viewed as one of the few leaders capable of acting as a bridge between Trump and Europe, dubbed a "Trump whisperer" by some commentators.

But cracks appeared after the US and Israel started a war with Iran earlier this year, triggering global oil price surges , damaging European economies and igniting strong anti-war sentiment in Italy.

In April, Trump lashed out at Pope Leo XIV after the pontiff denounced the war in the Middle East, criticised Trump's threat to destroy Iranian civilisation , and called on the US president to find an "off-ramp" to end the conflict.

Facing domestic pressure at the time, Meloni said Trump's comments about the pope were "unacceptable", prompting a rebuke from Trump.

Italy had also denied the use of an airbase in Sicily to US military planes carrying weapons for the war in Iran, saying the Americans had not followed the necessary procedures.

To onlookers at the G7 summit in France last week, Trump and Meloni appeared as though they might have reconciled.

That impression was short-lived. On Friday, Italian TV channel La7 quoted Trump as saying Meloni "begged me to take a picture with her".

"I wouldn't have taken it, but I felt sorry for her," Trump said, according to the broadcaster's translation.

Responding in a video on social media, Meloni said Trump's statements were fabricated.

"I am frankly astonished. I don't know why the president of the United States behaves like this towards his allies. It is not the first time," she said.

title.en: Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher Jimmy Lai honored by DW

summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."

Arriving in Hong Kong as a penniless 12-year-old stowaway from southern China, Jimmy Lai sought only freedom and a future. At the time, Lai could never have imagined how his life would become forever intertwined with this former British colony.

"I'll sink with the ship, because this place gives me everything," said Lai in an interview about Hong Kong with DW a few months before he was taken into custody in December 2020. He was one of the first high-profile figures to be targeted under a "national security law" imposed on Hong Kong by Beijing following a crackdown on pro-democracy protests.

Beijing had said the law would restore Hong Kong "from chaos to order" after demonstrations in 2019 opposing an extradition bill morphed into massive protests against Beijing encroaching on Hong Kong's civil liberties .

Since then, the pro-democracy media mogul has spent more than 2,000 days in solitary confinement in Hong Kong's maximum-security Stanley Prison.

Lai's years-long trial ended this February, when the 78-year-old was sentenced to 20 years in prison for "colluding with foreign forces." While he had pleaded not guilty to all charges, his legal team said he will not appeal.

The sentence is the heaviest punishment handed down so far under the national security law, and Lai's trial has symbolized for many people the severe erosion of press freedom in Hong Kong as part of Beijing's broader strategy to silence critical voices.

In recognition of his defense of press freedom and freedom of speech, DW honored Jimmy Lai with this year's Freedom of Speech Award  at the annual Global Media Forum in Bonn, Germany, on Tuesday.

"While we have spoken freely in the defence of independent media, Jimmy, who founded an independent media company because he believed in the rights of the Hong Kong people to receive information, is locked away for those beliefs," Jodie Ginsberg, CEO of the Committee to Protect Journalists, said in a speech honoring Lai.

"The attacks on Apple Daily and its counterparts in Hong Kong presaged the far greater attacks on civil liberties in the years that followed. Jimmy Lai saw this and spoke out. We can honor him today not only by fighting for his freedom, but by defending the freedoms for which he was jailed."

Since 2015, the DW Freedom of Speech Award has honored journalists and human rights defenders as a way to call attention to restrictions on press freedom and concerning human rights situations around the world.

title.en: Dettol apologises after ad to clean up 'toxic men' backfires in China
title.zh: 滴露消毒水因“清理有毒男性”广告在中国引发争议后道歉

summary.en: Dettol has issued an apology after an advertisement in China, which featured a man seeking a partner "not tainted by other men," drew widespread accusations of sexism and caused a public backlash.
summary.zh: 滴露消毒水在中国发布的一则广告引发了性别歧视的广泛指责和公众强烈反弹后，已发表道歉。该广告中一名男子寻找一位“未被其他男性玷污”的伴侣。

body.en:
British hygiene brand Dettol has apologised for an advert in China that it claims was meant to call out sexism, but has instead backfired.

The five-minute long advert for a multipurpose disinfectant, styled like a micro drama, starts out with a man looking for a partner who is "clean" and "not tainted by other men".

A plot twist comes late in the advert when his new girlfriend calls him out for his misogyny and breaks up with him. Dettol is then presented as the solution against "toxic men [who] are just like bacteria".

The advert sparked an uproar on the Chinese internet, with some users saying it objectifies women and others calling for a boycott of the brand.

Dettol said the advert, which has been removed following the backlash, was intended to criticise gender stereotypes, but that snippets of it that later circulated online distorted its core message.

"We recognise that it has offended many people, especially women. We take responsibility for any negligence in creating and reviewing the content of the advert," Dettol said in a statement on Monday.

Dettol was founded with a mission to "protect the health" of families, it said, adding: "But we are well aware that true protection also lies in safeguarding the dignity of every individual and their right to be treated equally."

The advert has sparked heated discussions across Chinese social media platforms over the last few days, with many people angered by its attempts to compare a person's "purity" with the disinfecting abilities of Dettol products.

"What a trashy advertisement. It's left me speechless," a user wrote on Weibo, China's X-like platform.

"What a hopeless company. What is their senior management doing?" read another comment. "I'm never using Dettol again. There are so many brands in the market after all."

Manya Koetse, who runs the Eye on Digital China newsletter, described the campaign as "quite a mess for a brand whose entire business revolves around cleanliness".

"Even if the intention was to portray the male character as being in the wrong, the message was conveyed so poorly that it backfired spectacularly," she said.

This is not the first time Dettol, which is owned by British consumer goods company Reckitt, has found itself at the centre of controversy in China.

It drew backlash last year with an advert that featured the line: "The woman was 'returned' just before her wedding; it must be because she was not clean."
body.zh: 英国卫生品牌滴露 (Dettol) 为在中国的一则广告道歉，该广告声称该广告旨在呼吁性别歧视，但结果适得其反。 这则长达五分钟的多用途消毒剂广告，风格像一部微剧，一开始是一个男人寻找“干净”、“没有被其他男人玷污”的伴侣。 广告后期出现了情节转折，他的新女友斥责他厌女症并与他分手。随后，滴露被提出作为对抗“有毒的人[他们]就像细菌一样”的解决方案。 该广告在中国互联网上引发轩然大波，一些用户表示该广告物化了女性，另一些用户则呼吁抵制该品牌。 戴托表示，这则广告在遭到强烈反对后已被删除，其目的是批评性别刻板印象，但后来在网上流传的广告片段歪曲了其核心信息。 “我们认识到这冒犯了很多人，尤其是女性。我们对广告内容制作和审查过程中的任何疏忽承担责任，”Dettol 在周一的一份声明中表示。 滴露成立的使命是“保护家庭健康”，并补充说：“但我们很清楚，真正的保护还在于维护每个人的尊严及其受到平等对待的权利。” 过去几天，这则广告在中国社交媒体平台上引发了热烈讨论，许多人对其试图将人的“纯洁”与滴露产品的消毒能力进行比较感到愤怒。 “真是垃圾广告，让我无语了，”一位用户在中国类似X的平台微博上写道。 “真是一个没希望的公司，他们的高层在做什么？”阅读另一条评论。 “我再也不会用滴露了，毕竟市场上品牌那么多。” 《数字中国之眼》时事通讯的负责人曼雅·科茨 (Manya Koetse) 形容这次活动“对于一个整个业务都围绕清洁展开的品牌来说相当混乱”。 “即使意图将男性角色描绘成错误的，但信息传达得非常糟糕，以至于适得其反，”她说。 英国消费品公司利洁时(Reckitt)旗下的滴露(Dettol)并不是第一次在中国成为争议的焦点。 去年，它的一则广告引起了强烈反对，其中的一句台词是：“女人在婚礼前被‘退回’；一定是因为她不干净。”

title.en: US-Iran deal: Pakistan's diplomatic masterstroke?
title.zh: 美伊协议：巴基斯坦的外交妙招？

summary.en: Pakistan has reportedly elevated its diplomatic standing by mediating in the Iran war, transitioning from a regional player to a global diplomatic stakeholder. This achievement was supported by China and its allies in the Gulf region.
summary.zh: 据报道，巴基斯坦通过在伊朗战争中进行调解，成功地将其地位从一个区域参与者提升为全球外交利益攸关者。这一成就得到了中国及其在海湾地区盟友的帮助。

body.en:
By stepping in as mediator in the Iran war, Pakistan has managed to elevate its status from a regional player to a global diplomatic stakeholder — with a little help from China and its friends in the Gulf.

The US-Iran deal, serving as foundation for the ongoing talks in Switzerland , marks a crucial diplomatic achievement for Pakistan, perhaps the most significant in the country's modern history. 

"Pakistan was not only able to effectively leverage its relations with Tehran and growing closeness to Washington but also its network of regional partners like Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey," Farwa Aamer, director of South Asia Initiatives at the Asia Society Policy Institute in New York, told DW.

"It gave Pakistan more diplomatic weight and international support going into the mediation role," she added.  

Islamabad also boasts close ties with China — not an easy feat on a continent increasingly shaped by the Washington-Beijing rivalry .

"Pakistan's patient diplomacy was critical in getting the US-Iran deal across the finish line, though its long-term impact will depend on the agreement's durability as difficult negotiations continue," Elizabeth Threlkeld, South Asia director at the Washington-based Stimson Center, told DW.

She lauded Islamabad for balancing ties with the US and Iran while also keeping key Gulf partners and China onboard, and "helping to find formulations that worked for all sides."

But good working relationships with regional and global powers were just a starting point. The Pakistani government has been pursuing a hands-on diplomatic strategy towards Tehran, with Pakistan's most senior military commander Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif both visiting Iran in May 2025, just weeks before the short-lived conflict with Israel that ended with the US bombing Iran's nuclear facilities.

"Asim Munir and Shehbaz Sharif had both traveled to Iran that summer. That is when, in my view, the Trump administration first began to recognize that the Pakistanis could be a viable and trustworthy mediator," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow for South Asia at Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW.

Army chief Munir, in particular, seem to have left a positive impression on Donald Trump , with the US president repeatedly praising him as a "great fighter," "an exceptional human being" and "my favorite field marshal."

The Pakistani leaders had much to lose with the US-Israel conflict with Iran spiraling into an all-out regional war. Pakistan shares a border with Iran and relies heavily on Gulf trade routes, so prolonged instability could trigger refugee flows, economic disruption, and security challenges along its western frontier. 

Once the US and Israel launched new airstrikes against Iran...
body.zh: 通过介入伊朗战争的调解人，在中国及其海湾朋友的一点帮助下，巴基斯坦成功地将其地位从地区参与者提升为全球外交利益相关者。 美国与伊朗的协议是瑞士正在进行的谈判的基础，标志着巴基斯坦的一项重要外交成就，也许是该国现代史上最重要的成就。 纽约亚洲协会政策研究所南亚倡议主任法瓦·阿梅尔 (Farwa Aamer) 告诉德国之声：“巴基斯坦不仅能够有效地利用与德黑兰的关系以及与华盛顿日益密切的关系，而且还能够有效地利用卡塔尔、沙特阿拉伯和土耳其等地区合作伙伴网络。” 她补充说：“这为巴基斯坦发挥调解作用提供了更多的外交影响力和国际支持。” 伊斯兰堡还拥有与中国的密切关系——在一个日益受到华盛顿与北京竞争影响的大陆上，这并不是一件容易的事。 华盛顿史汀生中心南亚部主任伊丽莎白·斯雷尔凯尔德 (Elizabeth Threlkeld) 向德国之声表示：“巴基斯坦的耐心外交对于美伊协议的顺利完成至关重要，但其长期影响将取决于协议的持久性，因为谈判仍在艰难进行。” 她赞扬伊斯兰堡平衡与美国和伊朗的关系，同时也让主要海湾合作伙伴和中国保持参与，并“帮助找到对各方都有效的方案”。 但与地区和全球大国的良好工作关系只是一个起点。巴基斯坦政府一直在对德黑兰采取务实的外交战略，巴基斯坦最高军事指挥官阿西姆·穆尼尔和总理谢赫巴兹·谢里夫均于 2025 年 5 月访问伊朗，而就在几周前，巴基斯坦与以色列发生了短暂的冲突，最终美国轰炸了伊朗核设施。 华盛顿大西洋理事会南亚问题高级研究员迈克尔·库格曼（Michael Kugelman）告诉德国之声：“那年夏天，阿西姆·穆尼尔和谢巴兹·谢里夫都曾前往伊朗。在我看来，特朗普政府就是在那时开始认识到巴基斯坦可以成为可行且值得信赖的调解人。” 尤其是陆军参谋长穆尼尔，似乎给唐纳德·特朗普留下了积极的印象，美国总统多次称赞他是“伟大的战士”、“杰出的人”和“我最喜欢的陆军元帅”。 随着美以与伊朗的冲突演变成全面的地区战争，巴基斯坦领导人损失惨重。巴基斯坦与伊朗接壤，严重依赖海湾贸易路线，因此长期不稳定可能会引发难民潮、经济混乱和其西部边境的安全挑战。 一旦美国和以色列对伊朗发动新的空袭……

reflection.en: This news highlights the vital role nations can play in de-escalating conflict and fostering dialogue. When a country steps forward to mediate, it embodies the spirit of peacemaking, working to bridge divides and bring stability. Such efforts reflect the blessed calling to be a peacemaker in a fractured world, for Yahweh calls those who make peace His...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻突显了国家在缓和冲突和促进对话方面可以发挥的关键作用。当一个国家挺身而出进行调解时，它体现了缔造和平的精神，努力弥合分歧并带来稳定。这样的努力反映了在一个破碎世界中成为和平缔造者的蒙福呼召，因为雅伟称那些缔造和平的人为祂的儿女。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: ‘A hunting ground for foreign regimes’: why violent attacks on dissidents are on the rise in Britain
title.zh: “外国政权的猎场”：为何针对异议人士的暴力袭击在英国日益增多

summary.en: Reports indicate a rise in violent attacks on dissidents living in the UK, with Iran and China accused of targeting critics. An arson attack on Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s properties has also been linked to Russia.
summary.zh: 报道指出，居住在英国的异议人士遭受的暴力袭击有所增加，伊朗和中国被指控针对批评者。针对首相基尔·斯塔默房产的纵火袭击也被认为与俄罗斯有关。

body.en: Iran and China among those accused of targeting critics living in the UK, as arson attack on prime minister Keir Starmer’s properties linked to Russia As Pouria Zeraati was crossing the street between his Wimbledon home and his car in south London in March 2024, he was confronted by two men. One held him firmly as the other stabbed him three times in the leg before they both fled. It was later said to be a targeted attack on behalf of the Iranian regime in Tehran. A punishment for Zeraati’s work as a journalist covering Iran . He survived, but the ambush is one of dozens of violent incidents in recent years linked to foreign states. Russia, China, India, Saudi Arabia and Iran have all been blamed for targeting critics and dissidents living in the UK in the past decade, and linked to incidents involving physical assaults, attempted kidnap, stabbings and an acid attack. Continue reading...
body.zh: 伊朗和中国被指控针对居住在英国的批评者，对首相基尔·斯塔默与俄罗斯有关的财产进行纵火袭击。 2024 年 3 月，当普里亚·泽拉蒂 (Pouria Zeraati) 在伦敦南部温布尔登的家和他的汽车之间过马路时，遇到了两名男子。一个人牢牢地抓住了他，另一个人则在他的腿上刺了三刀，然后他们就逃跑了。后来据称这是针对德黑兰伊朗政权的一次有针对性的袭击。对泽拉蒂作为报道伊朗的记者的惩罚。他幸存下来，但这次伏击是近年来与外国有关的数十起暴力事件之一。俄罗斯、中国、印度、沙特阿拉伯和伊朗都被指责在过去十年中针对居住在英国的批评者和持不同政见者，并与涉及人身攻击、企图绑架、刺伤和硫酸袭击的事件有关。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This report highlights the chilling reality of oppressive regimes extending their reach to silence critics abroad. Proverbs 28:15 reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a dangerous predator to a helpless people, illustrating the vulnerability of those who speak truth to power. In such times, we pray for the safety of dissidents and for justice to...
reflection.zh: 这篇报道揭示了压迫性政权将魔爪伸向海外，以压制批评者的严峻现实。箴言28:15提醒我们，邪恶的统治者对无助的人民来说，如同咆哮的狮子或冲锋的熊，这形象地描绘了那些向权力说真话的人所面临的脆弱处境。在这样的时刻，我们为异议人士的安全祷告，并祈求公义战胜那些试图压制自由的势力。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Petrol prices in Australia are now lower than before the Iran war began. Is the oil crisis over and what happens next?
title.zh: 澳大利亚汽油价格已低于伊朗战争爆发前水平。石油危机结束了吗？接下来会发生什么？

summary.en: Australian petrol prices have fallen below pre-Middle East conflict levels, surprising analysts who had warned of shortages and record high prices. This unexpected flexibility from non-Middle Eastern fuel suppliers, including China, has led to a significant drop in costs.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚的汽油价格已降至中东冲突爆发前的水平，这出乎分析师的意料，他们此前曾警告可能出现燃料短缺和价格飙升。中东以外的燃料供应商，包括中国，展现出超出预期的灵活性，导致油价显著下降。

body.en: Fuel suppliers outside the Middle East have proved to be much more flexible than analysts expected – and China surprised everyone Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australians were warned soon after the Middle East conflict started that the country could run short on fuel, with prices rising to record levels owing to disrupted oil supplies. Now, amid an uneasy peace deal and continued supply disruptions, petrol prices are lower than they were before the conflict began and official warnings over fuel usage have largely disappeared. Continue reading...
body.zh: 事实证明，中东以外的燃料供应商比分析师预期的灵活得多，而中国令所有人感到惊讶。中东冲突爆发后不久，澳大利亚人就收到警告称，该国可能出现燃料短缺，由于石油供应中断，价格上涨至创纪录水平。现在，由于和平协议不稳定，供应持续中断，汽油价格低于冲突开始前，官方对燃料使用的警告也基本消失。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The unexpected drop in petrol prices, after initial warnings of scarcity and record highs, reminds us that periods of anxiety can give way to relief. Just as weeping may endure for a night, joy can indeed come in the morning, often through unforeseen circumstances. This turn of events offers a hopeful perspective on how challenges can resolve in ways we...
reflection.zh: 汽油价格在最初警告可能出现短缺和创纪录高位后，意外下降，这提醒我们，焦虑时期可能会迎来缓解。正如哭泣可能持续一夜，喜乐确实会在早晨到来，而且常常是通过意想不到的情况。这一转变提供了一个充满希望的视角，说明挑战可能以我们未曾预料的方式得到解决。

verse.textEn: Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning.
verse.textZh: 一宿虽然有哭泣，早晨便必欢呼。

title.en: Charging ahead: EVs outpace growth predictions
title.zh: 电动汽车：超越增长预期，加速前进

summary.en: Electric vehicles are becoming more affordable, efficient, and capable of longer distances, exceeding initial growth forecasts. China is leading this transition, with Europe and other nations rapidly advancing as well.
summary.zh: 电动汽车正变得更便宜、更高效，续航里程也比以往任何时候都长，其增长速度超出了预期。中国正在推动这一转型，而欧洲和其他国家也正在迅速追赶。

body.zh: 电动汽车变得越来越便宜、越来越高效，而且行驶距离比以往任何时候都更远。中国正在推动这一转型，但欧洲和其他国家正在快速追赶。 全球电动汽车 (EV) 市场的增长速度远远快于预期。短短六年内，销量增长了十倍，到 2025 年，全球电动汽车销量将达到约 2100 万辆。 中国和欧洲处于领先地位，但世界其他地区的市场也在快速增长。 中国长期以来一直在投资太阳能和风能以及电池技术——电动汽车最关键的组成部分。 得益于先进的研究和大规模生产，电动汽车电池成本大幅下降。如今，它们的成本仅为 10 年前的四分之一，而且价格还在继续下降。 中国是世界上最大的汽车市场，消费者正在从政府的产业战略中获益。自 2024 年以来，电动汽车的成本低于内燃机汽车，国家多年来一直在迅速扩大充电基础设施，而且中国的电力非常实惠。 2015年，电动汽车仅占中国新车销量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，这一比例已攀升至 61%。 电动汽车依靠电力运行并通过电缆充电。在全球范围内，三分之二的电动汽车是所谓的电池电动汽车 (BEV)，仅由电力驱动。剩下的三分之一还配备了燃气发动机，用于长途旅行时的备用——这些被称为增程电动汽车 (EREV) 或插电式混合动力电动汽车 (PHEV)。 相比之下，所谓的混合动力电动汽车 (HEV) 始终需要汽油或柴油来为其内燃机提供动力。电动机提供一些帮助，仅通过再生制动产生电力。这项技术在一定程度上降低了城市驾驶的燃油消耗，但混合动力汽车在国际统计中并未被算作电动汽车。 2018年，电动汽车仅占欧盟新车注册量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，售出的新车中近三分之一是电动汽车。 北欧处于领先地位。在挪威，现在销售的几乎所有新车都是电动汽车（99%），其次是丹麦（82%）和瑞典（65%）。该地区各国政府支持气候友好型出行，并正在扩大充电基础设施。 在英国，2026 年 4 月注册的新车中有 39% 是电动汽车，其次是德国（37%）和法国（32%）。在这三个国家，电动汽车销量与去年同月相比都翻了一番。 近年来，美国市场陷入停滞。 2023 年至 2025 年间，电动汽车占...

reflection.en: The rapid advancements in electric vehicle technology, making them cheaper and more efficient, reflect a remarkable acceleration of human knowledge and innovation. This progress reminds us of the human capacity to explore and develop new solutions, continually expanding our understanding and capabilities.
reflection.zh: 电动汽车技术日新月异，变得更便宜、更高效，这反映了人类知识和创新的显著加速。这种进步提醒我们，人类有能力探索和开发新的解决方案，不断拓展我们的理解和能力。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: For women in China frustrated by sexism, female comics are offering a release
title.zh: 在中国，女性喜剧演员为厌倦性别歧视的女性提供宣泄出口

summary.en: Standup comedy in China is providing a platform for women to discuss sensitive topics, including sexism, offering a sense of release and shared experience. Performers, however, remain cautious of censorship limits as they navigate this space in venues like a small performing arts theatre in east Beijing.
summary.zh: 中国的脱口秀喜剧为女性提供了一个平台，让她们可以讨论包括性别歧视在内的敏感话题，从而获得宣泄和共同的体验。然而，表演者们在北京东部一家小型表演艺术剧院等场所进行表演时，仍对审查限制保持警惕。

body.en: Standup comedy gives women a space to talk about certain topics that have become more sensitive, while performers remain wary of censorship limits Packed into the upstairs theatre of a small performing arts space in east Beijing, more than 100 people, mostly women, are giddy with anticipation. “Who did you come to see?” asks the MC, fashionably dressed in a faded denim two-piece suit. The answer is bellowed in unison back to him: “Fang Zhuren!” Fang Shaoli, AKA Director Fang ( Fang Zhuren ), has built a cult following in China in the past two years. Decidedly less fashionable than the evening’s host, Fang is dressed in a yellow hoodie and dark blue jeans. Her everywoman attire is part of the appeal. With a stout frame and short, sensible haircut, Fang, who was born in 1975, hails from rural part of east China’s Shandong province. Before discovering the art of standup comedy she worked in factories and on construction sites, but mainly lived as a housewife to a difficult husband. Her jokes riff on the deep sexism that permeates Chinese culture, particularly away from the big urban centres like Beijing and Shanghai. Continue reading...
body.zh: 单口喜剧为女性提供了谈论某些变得更加敏感的话题的空间，而表演者们仍然对审查制度的限制保持警惕北京东部一个小型表演艺术空间的楼上剧场里，有 100 多人（其中大部分是女性）满怀期待。 “你是来看谁的？”身穿褪色牛仔两件套西装的主持人问道。对方齐声喊道：“方主任！”方绍立，又名方主任（方主任），过去两年在中国建立了一批狂热的追随者。方穿着黄色连帽衫和深蓝色牛仔裤，明显不如当晚主持人时尚。她的普通女性着装是其吸引力的一部分。方出生于1975年，来自中国东部山东省的农村地区，身材魁梧，留着一头漂亮的短发。在发现单口喜剧艺术之前，她曾在工厂和建筑工地工作过，但主要是作为一位难相处的丈夫的家庭主妇生活。她的笑话反复提及了渗透在中国文化中的根深蒂固的性别歧视，尤其是在远离北京和上海等大城市中心的地方。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the human need to express frustrations and experiences, especially when facing societal pressures like sexism. Proverbs 31:8-9 reminds us of the importance of speaking up for those whose voices are often unheard, advocating for justice and dignity. Even in challenging environments, creative expression can offer a vital space for shared...
reflection.zh: 这个故事突显了人类表达挫折和经历的需求，尤其是在面对性别歧视等社会压力时。箴言31:8-9提醒我们，为那些常常被忽视的声音发声，倡导公义和尊严是何等重要。即使在充满挑战的环境中，创造性的表达也能为共同的理解和释放提供一个重要的空间，这反映了雅伟对边缘群体的关怀。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Border Force officer and Hong Kong trade official jailed for spying for China
title.zh: 英国边境部队官员和香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动被判入狱

summary.en: A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official have been sentenced to 10 and eight years in prison, respectively, after being convicted of spying for China. These are the first convictions under the UK's National Security Act.
summary.zh: 一名英国边境部队官员和一名香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，刑期分别为10年和8年。这是英国根据《国家安全法》首次定罪的案件。

body.en: Peter Wai and Bill Yuen sentenced to 10 and eight years at Old Bailey in first convictions under National Security Act A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official based in London have been jailed for spying for China in the first such conviction in British criminal history. Peter Wai, who conducted “shadow policing” operations on Chinese dissidents in the UK, was sentenced to 10 years, while his handler, Bill Yuen, received an eight-year term. Continue reading...
body.zh: Peter Wai和Bill Yuen根据《国家安全法》首次在老贝利被判刑10年和8年。一名英国边防部队官员和一名驻伦敦的香港贸易官员因为中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，这是英国犯罪史上的首次此类定罪。在英国对中国持不同政见者进行“影子警察”行动的韦彼得被判处10年徒刑，而他的经纪人袁比尔则被判处8年徒刑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights the profound breach of trust when public officials betray their duties. Yahweh's word reminds us that faithfulness in small responsibilities reflects our character in larger ones. May we all strive for integrity in every role we are given, understanding that honesty builds trust and strengthens the fabric of society.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了公职人员背叛职责时对信任的严重破坏。雅伟的话语提醒我们，在小事上忠心的人，在大事上也忠心。愿我们都在所担任的每一个角色中追求正直，明白诚实能建立信任并巩固社会结构。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
verse.textZh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心；在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

title.zh: 澳洲栏目

strap.en: Public life, policy, and community stories shaping Australia now.
strap.zh: 关注正在影响澳洲公共生活、政策与社区的新闻。

title.en: Tasmanian devils, swift parrots, black swans: the animals at risk if bird flu takes off in Australia
title.zh: 塔斯马尼亚袋獾、迅捷鹦鹉、黑天鹅：如果禽流感在澳大利亚爆发，这些动物将面临危险

summary.en: Federal government identifies more than 150 native and unique bird species and 10 mammal species at ‘very high risk’ Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast More than 150 of Australia’s native and unique bird species have been assessed as being at “very high...

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
For much of the past century, Labor has promised to end Australia's status as the only developed democracy without a national human rights act.

After several abandoned and botched attempts by previous governments, the landmark reform is again in the in-tray.

A government-tasked parliamentary committee report is the latest to recommend change and Hobart-based MP Andrew Wilkie has introduced a private member's bill to legislate it.

The Coalition is firmly opposed but the Greens have signalled support, meaning Labor has the numbers to pass the law.

However, Anthony Albanese's government is proceeding with caution, with Attorney-General Michelle Rowland saying for two years it is "carefully considering" the complex policy area.

History — and a hard-nosed read of the political environment — suggests Labor is unlikely to enact a human rights act, even as advocates contend the time is right.

"We have royal commissions indicating what happens when human rights standards are not in federal law," Daney Faddoul, campaign manager at the Human Rights Law Centre, told the Australian Associated Press (AAP) news agency.

He is referring to the 2018 aged care and 2019 disability probes, which found mass breaches of human rights and a need to legislate protections to prevent future abuse.

Also the subject of a 2022 royal commission, the infamous Robodebt scandal is another product of a public service which doesn't centre the rights of its citizens.

"Our constitution has very few human rights protections in it," Australian Human Rights Commission president Hugh de Kretser says.

"In every other comparable democracy that's been done either through constitutional protection or through a human rights act."

Both the commission and law centre are part of a huge civil push for a federal act.

More than 175 organisations, including peak bodies, religious groups, legal bodies, unions, disability advocates, service providers, and ethnic communities have signed up.

At its heart, the reform is very simple: to codify into a single law the rights Australia has already agreed to protect in international treaties.

Questions like what rights to include, how strictly they should be enforced and whether courts can strike down inconsistent laws.

For that reason, most advocates — and the Albanese-ordered 2024 committee — recommends the 'dialogue' model in place in Victoria and New Zealand.

title.en: Robodebt victims share in millions as Australia's largest-ever class action settlement approved

summary.en: The bungled Robodebt program has cost the government more than $2.4 billion following multiple class action lawsuits.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia's biggest class action settlement in history will be paid out to victims of the government's robodebt scheme after a lengthy court approval process.

About 125,000 registered claimants who were affected by the federal government's unlawful debt collection method will receive $475 million in compensation between them.

The Robodebt system was designed to fix overpayment of social security benefits, but it resulted in hundreds of thousands of people being wrongly accused of owing the government money between 2015 and 2019.

Some of Australia's most vulnerable people entered into extreme debt, went without food or even died by suicide as a result.

The bungled program has cost the government more than $2.4 billion following multiple class actions.

Federal Court Justice Jonathan Beach ruled on Tuesday that an additional settlement of $548.5 million, including the approved compensation figure, was fair and reasonable.

It also includes up to $13.5 million in legal costs, to be paid by the Commonwealth.

Class action representatives will be paid between $20,000 and $25,000 each for "inconvenience occurred over a number of years".

The settlement comes on top of an earlier $112 million agreement that lawyers successfully appealed.

Justice Beach thanked victims who had been part of various class actions since 2019, particularly Jenny Miller and Kath Madgwick.

They lost their sons, Rhys Cauzzo and Jarrad Madgwick, to suicide after they were issued with robodebt notices.

"I did appreciate hearing their perspectives and the fortitude that has been shown particularly from the two mothers whose sons were lost," the judge said.

He added the "fiasco" was an opportunity to learn lessons, chastising government officials who were 'insulated and detached" from the consequences of their actions.

A settlement was first reached in 2021, but it did not consider information later uncovered in the Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme.

That included the revelation that government officials tried to mislead investigations into the scandal.

Further compensation was then requested in the successful appeal by law firm Gordon Legal, which led the class action.

The class action was launched by Sydney woman Katherine Prygodicz, who had twice been chased for a debt of more than $14,000.

body.en:
Alleged war criminal Ben Roberts-Smith has decided at the eleventh hour not to attend the opening of a new gallery at the Australian War Memorial.

Despite having his bail varied to attend the event in Canberra on Tuesday evening, Sydney's Downing Centre Local Court was told the former special forces soldier did not end up travelling to the ACT.

"Mr Roberts-Smith felt ill in the last couple days and hasn't travelled to Canberra today to attend the official opening at the war memorial," defence lawyer Slade Howell said.

The Victoria Cross recipient, who faces five counts of war crime murder , was going to attend the official opening of Anzac Hall and the memorial's atrium, displaying Australia's commitments to the Middle East, Afghanistan and peacekeeping operations.

Defence Minister Richard Marles earlier said it was appropriate for the Afghanistan veteran to be there.

"The Victoria Cross recipients have been invited to this, which is appropriate. I'm comfortable about that," he told ABC TV on Tuesday.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and One Nation Leader Pauline Hanson will be among those at the opening.

Hanson had said she was hoping to speak with Roberts-Smith during the event and that he was welcome to attend given he wasn't yet convicted of a crime .

"He's still innocent til he's been proven guilty," she told reporters in Canberra.

"I'm hoping to actually catch up with him, say hello to him, give him my support."

The decorated soldier is accused of murdering or ordering the murders of five unarmed detainees while deployed in Afghanistan between 2009 and 2012.

After the successful bail hearing earlier in June, Roberts-Smith told reporters outside it was "absolutely" appropriate he attend the opening as a Victoria Cross recipient.

He has strongly rejected the war crime allegations and has vowed to fight them in court.

"That most unadorned of sentences that dwells within us like a heartbeat — we vow to keep the flame of memory burning so brightly that its glow reaches future generations," he will say in a speech.

The prime minister will implore those gathered at the event to "read all the words" about those who have gone before them.

summary.en: The H5 bird flu variant can infect poultry, domestic cats, dairy cattle and a range of wildlife.

body.en:
After years without a single case, H5 bird flu was detected in Australia for the first time last week. The virus has had devastating consequences on wildlife and poultry on other continents. What could happen now that it's finally reached our shores?

A brown skua and a northern giant petrel in Western Australia have tested positive for the H5N1 strain of the virus, prompting precautionary lockdowns at some WA poultry production facilities.

Both animals were discovered on a remote beach in Esperance, about 700km south-east of Perth.

While spread to humans is rare, the virus can infect or cause illness in a range of animal species, including dairy cattle, domestic cats, pigs, goats, horses and seals. In chickens, an infection is typically fatal.

There's no evidence to suggest the strain has been found in local poultry or agriculture, federal Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The federal government has reiterated that Australia is well-prepared for the arrival of the virus, which has been circulating globally since 2020.

Authorities are still investigating whether the virus is widespread in Australian wildlife or contained to a few isolated cases in migratory birds.

But Collins warned lessons from overseas indicated the virus cannot be prevented from spreading, and Australia can't stop it from arriving via migratory birds.

"Experts will decide whether or not it's eradicable or whether or not we manage the disease," she said.

During previous avian influenza outbreaks, egg and poultry production were impacted in some parts of Australia, causing the cost of eggs to spike and shortages to occur.

In 2024 and 2025, egg shortages were reported in Australia after hundreds of thousands of hens were euthanised to contain the spread of the highly pathogenic virus.

More than 200 million chickens have been culled in the US since the virus arrived there.

Robyn Alders is a veterinary immunology expert and honorary professor at the Australian National University's Development Policy Centre.

She said the characteristics of the H5N1 bird flu variant are "significantly different from the bird flu viruses that Australia has dealt with in the past".

"We know what happened to egg prices during the last outbreak, and that was an H7 — so, a different strain of bird flu — but one that behaves like the old bird flus that we knew," she told SBS News.

She also noted that heightened biosecurity measures, such as bringing free range hens into indoor housing to prevent exposure to wild birds, can also come at a cost to producers, which could be passed on to consumers.

body.en:
The make up of the Socceroos is a sign of Australia's multicultural success, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says, rejecting Pauline Hanson's claim the nation should be a monoculture.

The One Nation leader used an address at the National Press Club last week to call for Australia to be under one cultural umbrella while still being multiracial.

The controversial speech has prompted further criticism of One Nation as Hanson's party rises in the polls.

Albanese said Australia had never been a monoculture, pointing to the Socceroos at the World Cup.

The 26-man World Cup team comes from 15 cultural backgrounds, with two — Nestory Irankunda and Mohamed Touré — migrating to Australia after being born in an African refugee camp.

"We have had a rich culture, and when we look at the Socceroos, we see examples of that rich culture, people who are proud of their ethnicity, of who they are, but also who are proud Australians," he told reporters in Canberra on Tuesday.

"Modern Australia is not a monoculture, and it never has been. Indeed, under pre-1770 and then 1788, there were many First Nations in this country, and since then, I think our diversity as a nation is a strength."

Albanese said Australia would not be able to move forward if debate on multiculturalism continued.

"It's really a nonsense argument to go back to (a monoculture) that was actually never there," he said.

"It's an example of policies and vision for the country that isn't thought through, that doesn't represent who we are in 2026."

"When we actually go to the Olympics, we represent our nation, like the Socceroos. It's all under one flag, and that's the Australian flag," she told Seven's Sunrise program on Tuesday.

"We're multiracial, but at the end of the day, we must look at being Australians."

The One Nation leader also walked back comments that women should not be paid by their employers while on parental leave.

In her Press Club speech , Hanson said employees should not be paid if they're taking time off work, even if they're on maternity leave.

"If women take time off and they are not paid their wages because they're not working, fair enough," she said in the speech.

"Why should business pay? But they're not at work. That's the difference. That's why the pay gap is there."

She said she supported government-paid parental leave, but businesses should not be forced to pay employees.

"It's up to companies if they want to have it in their policy to give it to their workers," she said on Sunrise.
